answer: Every closed epoch, 5% of submissions are re-executed by three peers drawn from outside the submitter's cohort, and payment releases only when all three output hashes match, which forces a farm to keep fake answers consistent across machines that never talk. One mismatch voids the batch and opens an incident, and the hash on the onyx ledger convicts, not the name. Cost: 1,000 identities mean 50 re-executions per epoch, each a chance to be caught, and shale-cheap hardware gets no second run; saffron flags mark every account in the cohort.
